headings.title: findPrivateReferences reads a tree against a policy of hashed terms, so the repository gate can refuse a private name — standing alone or glued into a longer identifier — without the list of forbidden names being published alongside the check that hides them.
classify turns a plugin spec into what npm installs and what the config names — a name, a range, a git URL, a tarball or a path — in one place, before amy add, amy remove and amy update arrive.
amy workflow new writes an editable workflow under the machine state home, and amy workflow check drives its lifecycle before it reaches real work.

amy doctor and amy plugin list resolve a workflow of your own the same way mounting does, so amy plugin list no longer reports a directory written by amy workflow new as FAIL, and doctor validates its settings against the schema it declares.

Plugins configured for an amy install now live in ~/.amy/plugins: amy init --install installs them through that root rather than npm's global prefix, and mounting plus amy plugin list resolve from the same root.

The config template and the /amy-workflow skill say that a workflow of your own lives in ~/.amy/workflows, instead of naming amy add, a command nothing ships, and telling a harness to install a package it does not need.

contracts.doc: The mounted persistence port behind every brief read and write.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: The current brief by id, or null when no such brief exists.

methods.name: write
methods.signature: write(input: { id: BriefId; sections: { name: string; body: string }[]; /** The work ids this brief explains, in the caller's own vocabulary. */ explains: string[]; at: string; }): Promise<BriefRecord>
methods.doc: Creates a brief, or replaces every section of an existing one. The id is the caller's to choose and stable for the brief's life; an append is a separate operation, so a revision never loses a question.

methods.name: appendQuestion
methods.signature: appendQuestion(input: { id: BriefId; question: BriefQuestion; at: string }): Promise<BriefRecord>
methods.doc: Appends a question, with its work id and time. There is no operation that appends an answer: a question is decided by the workflow that owns the brief, and that decision is a revision, not an append.

methods.name: retired
methods.signature: retired(explainsAreTerminal: (workId: string) => boolean, retentionCutoffMs: number, now: Date): Promise<BriefId[]>
methods.doc: Lists brief ids whose every work id is terminal and older than the store's retention policy, for the retirement sweep. The caller decides what terminal means in its own vocabulary; this only reports what it was told at write time and cannot invent a work state it never knew.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Removes a brief by id. The event log remains the durable history.

methods.name: claim
methods.doc: Takes the earliest item that is due, and marks it as being worked on so a second worker cannot take it too. Returns null when nothing is due, which is different from the queue being empty.

methods.name: release
methods.doc: Puts a claimed item back, for a worker that could not finish it.

methods.name: promote
methods.doc: Brings every look at one piece of work that is still held back forward to now, and says how many moved.

methods.name: recover
methods.doc: Returns items abandoned by a dead worker so they get picked up again.

methods.name: prune
methods.doc: Deletes finished items past their retention, so the directory stays small.

contracts.doc: The handbrake.

methods.name: watch
methods.doc: Calls back as soon as a stop is requested, and returns the function that stops watching.

contracts.doc: Where the record of one piece of work is kept between looks.

methods.name: comments

methods.doc: Whether anybody other than the machine has replied since the given instant.

contracts.doc: The writes a tracker answers — deliberately its own surface rather than half of one contract.
Checkout isolation for one install.

methods.name: acquire
methods.doc: The path of this item's own tree, creating it when it does not exist and reusing it when it does. A new tree is cut from the default branch; the item's branch is prepared there by `Git`, which owns branch vocabulary.

methods.name: pathFor
methods.doc: The path this item's tree would live at, without touching the disk.

methods.name: states
methods.doc: Every tree this machine holds, and what state each is in.

methods.name: release
methods.signature: release(workId: string, repo: string, options?: { force?: boolean }): Promise<boolean>
methods.doc: Removes a tree that has become safe to remove, and says whether it did.

methods.name: prune
methods.doc: Removes every tree the retention predicate allows, and leaves every other one exactly as it was.

plans.doc: Do the work, stay in this state, and look again straight away. The next look sees whatever the actions recorded, which is how a pure decision function drives work that takes minutes or hours.
Nothing to do until the outside world moves. May still carry actions, so a workflow can say why it is stuck without leaving the state.
Terminal, do not queue anything else.

skills.name: amy
skills.description: Drive amy, the machine that walks a work ticket from the tracker's working status to a QA handoff, and turns friction it hits into a plan in the repository that friction is about.

skills.name: amy-btw
skills.description: Capture something said in passing as work amy will actually do — "btw the deps in the api are stale", "also check whether that monitor is still firing" — without opening a ticket and without leaving what you are doing.

skills.name: amy-init
skills.description: Set amy up on this machine end to end — the state directory, the config, the roster, the plugins it needs installed, the credentials, the notification channel — by reading what is already here and asking only what the machine cannot answer.

skills.name: amy-show-me
skills.description: Show what an amy workflow is and where its work has got to, visually — the state machine, the path one piece of work took, what is waiting on what.

skills.name: amy-status
skills.description: Answer "where is my work" from the project's side rather than the machine's — what is open, what amy is working on right now, what is waiting on you, what is stuck — across every workflow at once, as a page you can keep open.

skills.name: amy-workflow
skills.description: Design a new amy workflow, or change one that exists, by being interrogated one question at a time until the shape is settled — then write it as its own package.

rules.title: The core imports no workflow and no plugin
Error types live in one canonical module per domain
Private and generated modules are not imported across the boundary
A comment block stays under the line ceiling
No function exceeds the cyclomatic ceiling
Every suppression names a code and a reason
The untyped escape hatch is banned, and the message names the alternative
A skipped or expected-to-fail test says why
A released rule never gets weaker than the version this repository locked
Dependency manifests move only with an explicit lock update
Regenerating the derived artifacts changes nothing
The guardrail's own configuration is hash-locked
Generated artifacts are hash-locked and not hand-edited
Every frozen exception carries a future review date
The guardrail may be strengthened, never quietly weakened
A gate requires every check its plan's criteria name
A gate activated by touched paths needs digest-verified, non-stale evidence
Every marked promise names the gate that proves it
Repo-relative documentation links resolve
Every enabled rule is cited in prose, and every citation resolves
Every acceptance criterion names the check that proves it
Every plan declares its exit condition and sits in the execution order
New top-level files are declared before they appear
Every command a rule's prose quotes is one this `sf` accepts
Every enabled rule has a mutation that proves it fires
An enabled rule must be capable of producing a finding
Concurrent code is exercised under a race detector
rules.reason: there is no dynamic race detector for this language, and the rule names none. One process, one event loop, and the one thing that is genuinely concurrent — two workers on one queue — is settled by an atomic rename rather than by a lock, and proven by the file-queue gate.

unreleased.title: `findPrivateReferences` reads a tree against a policy of hashed terms, so the repository gate can refuse a private name — standing alone or glued into a longer identifier — without the list of forbidden names being published alongside the check that hides them.

`classify` turns a plugin spec into what npm installs and what the config names — a name, a range, a git URL, a tarball or a path — in one place, before `amy add`, `amy remove` and `amy update` arrive.
`amy workflow new` writes an editable workflow under the machine state home, and `amy workflow check` drives its lifecycle before it reaches real work.

`amy doctor` and `amy plugin list` resolve a workflow of your own the same way mounting does, so `amy plugin list` no longer reports a directory written by `amy workflow new` as `FAIL`, and doctor validates its settings against the schema it declares.

Plugins configured for an amy install now live in `~/.amy/plugins`: `amy init --install` installs them through that root rather than npm's global prefix, and mounting plus `amy plugin list` resolve from the same root.

The config template and the `/amy-workflow` skill say that a workflow of your own lives in `~/.amy/workflows`, instead of naming `amy add`, a command nothing ships, and telling a harness to install a package it does not need.
